request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 39.4% (95% band 32.6% to 47.8%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.42; 1: +0.7; >= 2: +2.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.50, 95% band [+2.41, +2.70]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 20.3% (95% band 16.8% to 23.0%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 79999: +0.46; 80000-159999: +0.08; >= 160000: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.02, 95% band [-1.24, -0.88]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.1% (95% band 6.2% to 11.3%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 4199: +0.0597; >= 4200: -0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.40, 95% band [-0.63, -0.28]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 7.6% (95% band 3.4% to 9.1%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 9893: -0.14; >= 9894: +0.05 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.60, 95% band [+0.29, +0.79]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.5% (95% band 2.1% to 8.0%); rank 4 to 7 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.21 (95% band [-0.38, -0.06]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 19,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 3.4% (95% band 0.9% to 5.3%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.21 (95% band [+0.04, +0.35]) from x = 23 (5th percentile) to x = 53 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.1% to 2.8%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.10, 95% band [+0.00, +0.16]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.2% to 4.2%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.05, 95% band [-0.00, +0.33]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.1% (95% band 0.0% to 2.1%); rank 8 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.07, +0.12]).

Interactions: the model has 25 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 1.2% to 3.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.35 (95% band +2.17 to +2.59) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.49 (95% band +2.36 to +2.80) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.07 (95% band -1.38 to -0.92) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.93 (95% band -1.19 to -0.64) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.2% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.11 (95% band -1.37 to -0.91) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -0.89 (95% band -1.15 to -0.77) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.39 (95% band -0.59 to -0.16) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.17 (95% band -0.37 to -0.01) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.7% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.29 (95% band +2.07 to +2.47) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.58 (95% band +2.38 to +2.74) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.41 (95% band +0.05 to +0.64) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.70 (95% band +0.44 to +0.91) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.1% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.36 (95% band -0.72 to -0.26) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.56 (95% band -0.85 to -0.33) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.21 (95% band -0.00 to +0.53) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.01 (95% band -0.08 to +0.38) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.3% to 1.8%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.03 (95% band -1.34 to -0.80) when `AGE` = 23, -1.15 (95% band -1.32 to -0.91) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.30 (95% band +0.08 to +0.48) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.18 (95% band -0.00 to +0.43) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.53 (95% band +0.26 to +0.77) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.63 (95% band +0.29 to +0.80) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.25 (95% band -0.45 to -0.08) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.15 (95% band -0.35 to -0.05) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.2% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.92 (95% band -1.25 to -0.78) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.06 (95% band -1.31 to -0.88) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.32 (95% band -0.63 to -0.20) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.46 (95% band -0.65 to -0.28) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 0.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.45 (95% band -0.64 to -0.28) when `AGE` = 23, -0.36 (95% band -0.66 to -0.24) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.19 (95% band +0.04 to +0.36) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.28 (95% band +0.05 to +0.43) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
- `PAY_0 & AGE`: share of importance 0.7% (95% band 0.1% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.48 (95% band +2.34 to +2.70) when `AGE` = 23, +2.53 (95% band +2.40 to +2.82) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.22 (95% band +0.04 to +0.36) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.27 (95% band +0.07 to +0.49) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.47 (95% band +2.38 to +2.67) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +2.54 (95% band +2.38 to +2.79) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.23 (95% band -0.40 to -0.07) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.16 (95% band -0.31 to +0.01) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.1% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.66 (95% band +0.31 to +0.94) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.61 (95% band +0.27 to +0.76) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.42 (95% band -0.66 to -0.27) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.47 (95% band -0.83 to -0.31) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.2% to 1.3%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.51 (95% band +2.36 to +2.77) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.56 (95% band +2.23 to +2.72) when `PAY_AMT1` = 18,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 18,400: -0.41 (95% band -0.65 to -0.28) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.36 (95% band -0.86 to -0.25) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- 13 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 2.1%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the repayment status in the latest month, September 2005: this single feature accounts for about 39% of the model's importance, and applicants already one or more months behind on payments carry much higher predicted default risk."},{"id":2,"text":"The amount of credit granted (the credit limit) is the second most important driver, at about 20% of importance; smaller limits (below 160,000 NT dollars) are associated with higher predicted risk, and larger limits with lower risk."},{"id":3,"text":"The September payment amount, the September bill amount, and the August payment amount each matter less, at roughly 5 to 8% of importance each, and the direction of their effects is less certain because their uncertainty bands are wide."},{"id":4,"text":"Age matters only modestly: predicted risk rises somewhat with age from about 23 to 53, but this effect is small and its uncertainty band is wide, so it should not be treated as a strong driver."},{"id":5,"text":"Education and the earlier bill and payment amounts contribute little, and the data do not settle whether they affect predictions at all."},{"id":6,"text":"The effect of repayment status is somewhat stronger for applicants with smaller credit limits than for those with larger ones, meaning the two features interact, though this interaction is small in size."},{"id":7,"text":"Other pairwise interactions, such as those between credit limit and age or between repayment status and age, are each small, so the model's predictions are best understood mainly through repayment status and credit limit."}]}
